request: Hey Claude, I just added the "pricing-research-survey" skill. We raised House Blend from $14 to $16 on September 1 and ran a price survey in October. Analyse the survey, tell me if the price change hurt sales, and recommend the price to test next. Unit cost is $7.40 a bag.
business: Example Roasters, an online coffee roaster (invented example)
product: House Blend whole bean coffee, 340 g bag

price_change.product: House Blend whole bean coffee, 340 g bag

inputs_from_user.control_products: every other coffee on the store (prices unchanged from August to September)

sources.survey: Google Sheets, tab "Responses", read with list_sheets, get_sheet_peak and query_sheet_data
sources.orders: Shopify get_orders (status any) for both windows, summarised by day; promotions from get_price_rules
sources.rivals: rival product pages, prices pasted by the user on 2026-10-28

survey.product_card: House Blend whole bean coffee, 340 g bag, roasted to order and shipped within 2 days.

questions.too_cheap: At what price per bag would it seem so cheap you would doubt the quality?
questions.bargain: At what price per bag would it feel like a great deal?
questions.getting_expensive: At what price per bag would it start to feel expensive, though you would still consider it?
questions.too_expensive: At what price per bag would it be too expensive to consider?
questions.ladder: How likely are you to buy one bag at $X? (1 definitely not, 5 definitely would)
questions.attention: To show you are reading, pick 'Sometimes'.

note: Example data: an invented online coffee roaster with invented survey answers, orders and rivals, not a real business. Every number in expected_output.json follows from this input.
